claims.claim: Page title: Generate regression scenarios from production sessions
promptarena generate is a command with a --source flag taking an adapter name
--source pulls sessions from the platform the deploy adapter targets
generate writes one scenario per session
generate works best for one-shot and agent-loop sessions
The first user input becomes the scenario's turn
Agent behaviour after the input (tool calls, workflow transitions, final answer) becomes assertions
Later user turns in long multi-turn sessions are written against recorded answers and may not reproduce
generate keeps every turn for multi-turn sessions and warns
The warning appears both in command output and in the scenario description
Deploy adapter must have the sessions capability
promptarena deploy adapter install omnia installs the omnia adapter
An older adapter is reported with the exact install command to run
Arena config accepts a deploy: section
promptarena deploy login command issues the token used by generate
The adapter receives the same merged profile that deploy apply uses for the default environment (endpoint, workspace, token).
promptarena deploy apply command exists
--workspace flag on generate overrides the workspace from the profile
Example: promptarena generate with --source omnia, --config arena.yaml, --filter-passed=false, --output scenarios/production
--source is the adapter name, e.g. omnia
--config flag on generate takes the arena config file
--filter-passed is a boolean flag on generate
--output flag on generate sets the output directory
--filter-passed=false selects sessions with a failed recorded verdict
--expect flag on generate accepts an eval expression such as faithfulness>=0.8
Example: generate with --expect faithfulness>=0.8 and --output scenarios/faithfulness
--expect selects on a measurement and states the expected range
--expect faithfulness>=0.8 selects sessions where faithfulness scored below 0.8 or was never measured
Generated scenarios assert min_score: 0.8 for faithfulness
Real sessions record measurements (scores), not verdicts
generate prints one line per recorded eval describing what it became and why
Decision line shows eval decision 'asserted-expectation' with min_score and reason 'user expectation'
Decision line 'reported' with the hint to pass --expect <eval>>=<value> (or <=) or declare threshold in the pack
--expect accepts the <= operator as well as >=
An eval can declare a threshold in the pack
Eval with a failed recorded verdict is asserted with its recorded params
Eval with a passed recorded verdict is dropped
Pack (--config) threshold for an eval causes it to be asserted with that bound
--expect for an eval causes it to be asserted with that bound
Eval with no verdict, threshold or --expect is reported and never asserted against an invented bound
Generated scenarios are plain YAML scenario files that can be edited by hand
Redaction happens upstream in the platform before session data is served; the generator performs none
generate.Generate is a library function that takes a SessionSourceAdapter
generate.SessionSourceAdapter is an exported interface type
Generate returns scenarios in memory with per-eval decisions
flow.OpenSessionSource wraps an installed deploy adapter as a SessionSourceAdapter
An in-process platform can implement SessionSourceAdapter against its own store and call Generate directly
Generate re-checks ListOptions.Expectations against every session it fetches
Sessions that fail the expectation check land in Result.Skipped
arena/generate exports ViolatesAny for the expectation check
arena/generate exports UserTurnIndex to number evals by the user turn they answer
arena/generate exports EvalResultsFromRows to map stored records to eval results
arena/generate exports HasFailedVerdict for a summary's HasFailures
Session summary has a HasFailures field
SessionDetail is the type stored records are mapped onto
An in-process source and a deploy adapter using the shared helpers produce the same scenarios from the same records
promptarena generate has no --env flag; it merges the default environment's profile.
